summary: Client path migration causes silent tail and interleaved partial JSON fragments during SSE reconnect
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report SSE streams that appear to terminate silently after a short network path migration (e.g., mobile -> wifi) and, on reconnect, the resumed session contains interleaved partial JSON fragments instead of a clean continuation. Impact: customers see truncated final sentences or corrupted JSON payloads, causing downstream parsers to fail.

Impact:
- Korvo Media (dedicated) observed ~18% of streaming requests during a 3 hour window dropped final paragraph or returned invalid JSON after reconnect.
- Product features that expect structured JSON choices fail to render the final block.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated, customer pool rdx-ded-02 (us-east)
- API: /v1/stream (SSE) with auth token scoped to Korvo account
- Client: Korvo mobile app v2.4.1 using native SSE client with keepalive and automatic reconnect
- Observed during cellular->wifi handoffs and when edge proxy path migration occurs

Steps to reproduce (observed / customer steps):
1) Start SSE streaming request against gpt-redwood-rlf-2.7b with long output (>= 600 tokens).
2) While stream is active, trigger network path change (disable cellular, enable WiFi) or simulate path migration via network emulator that changes source IP.
3) Client reconnects using same session token and attempts resume.
4) Client receives a tail of the previous stream (heartbeat or partial chunk) and the resumed stream includes fragments like '{"choices": [{"text": "...in conclusion"}]}' (truncated) followed by a new fragment from resumed response, producing interleaved JSON tokens.

Logs / Observables:
- Proxy logs (edge-proxy-us-east-3) show a GOAWAY / path-migrate entry followed by a 101 upgrade for a new connection within 200-400ms.
- Serving runtime trace (trace_id=tr-20260310-9982) shows request rung up on worker-7 then a reconnect pinned to worker-12 after path migration. KV cache priming occurs on worker-12 but a stale end-marker from worker-7 is delivered before resume chunks.
- Client-side stacktrace (Korvo) shows JSON decode error: "Unexpected end of JSON input" at resume boundary.

Relevant links:
- Slack thread: #support (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05SUPPORT/thread-2026-03-10)
- Incident note (internal): INC-2026-03-10-07
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821
steps_to_reproduce: Start a long SSE stream (>600 tokens) to /v1/stream using the customer's dedicated pool
Trigger a client network path migration (cellular -> wifi) while stream is active
Allow the client to reconnect and resume using the same session token
Observe the resumed stream for interleaved partial JSON fragments and final sentence loss

comments: Asha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reports 18% failure rate for long streams during mobile handoffs. Attached client logs and example payloads.

Ravi Kapoor (SRE) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally using tc/netem path migration; observed that worker handoff sometimes emits a trailing partial chunk flagged as 'end' before KV cache priming completes on new worker.

Eleni Morris (Serving Eng) 2026-03-11: Hypothesis: resume protocol does not strictly enforce 'end' marker origin; if a stale 'end' is delivered from previous worker and followed by resume chunks, client-side parsers see interleaved JSON. Adding to backlog to add origin tagging to end markers.
Korvo Support Contact (Martin Li) 2026-03-11: We can throttle reconnects for now but need a more reliable fix; this affects our live-captions feature.
investigation_notes: 03/11: Reproduced with netem delaying 300-500ms between connections; race window appears when handoff time < 600ms.

03/11: Worker handoff path: controller issues a 'handoff' message to new worker and old worker sends final chunks then exits. Final chunk may be buffered by edge proxy and delivered after new worker's resume stream begins.
03/11: KV cache priming on target worker takes ~80-120ms for long context; resume transparent when priming completes before any buffered tail is flushed.
03/12: Edge proxy (envoy) configuration shows connection_coalescing enabled and keepalive probes are set to 10s; observed earlier GOAWAYs during path migration which flush buffered writes.
03/12: Added verbose trace to serving runtime to tag end-markers with origin-worker-id; observed cases where origin id differs between end fragment and subsequent resume chunks.
resolution_notes: Workaround (customer-facing): Instructed Korvo to implement a client-side parser tolerant to partial fragments at resume boundaries (ignore trailing incomplete object until a valid end marker is observed). Not ideal but reduces crashes.
Temporary mitigation (platform): Disabled connection_coalescing on edge-proxy-us-east-3 for Korvo's pool to reduce buffered tail delivery. This reduced error rate to ~3% in the next 6h window.

Planned fix: Engineering to implement origin-tagging of terminal markers and require an explicit resume ACK from client before resuming stream content on new worker. PR #4821 adds end-marker worker-id tagging and a short jittered hold-window to ensure cache priming. ETA: 2026-03-20 for internal rollout to dedicated pools.

Follow-ups: Add automated test covering netem path migration scenario and update runbook with 'disable coalescing' mitigation steps. Notify accounts team when fix is deployed to schedule verification with Korvo.
